title: Strategic Assets Protection Act
latestAction: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on Foreign Affairs, and Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary:
Strategic Assets Protection Act

This bill requires the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) to review real estate, business, and other transactions completed since 2017 that involve U.S. nuclear triad sites. (The United States maintains a triad of strategic nuclear delivery vehicles, which includes long-range land-based intercontinental ballistic missiles, long-range submarine-launched ballistic missiles on strategic nuclear submarines, and long-range heavy bombers.)

Specifically, CFIUS must review of all transactions completed on or after January 1, 2017, that involve real estate, businesses, critical infrastructure, or assets located within, adjacent to, or functionally supporting facilities that host, maintain, modernize, test, command, or control components of the U.S. nuclear triad. This includes, among other elements, weapons storage areas, communications infrastructure, and production or research facilities of the National Nuclear Security Administration.

The review must include an assessment of whether a transaction presents a risk to U.S. national security and whether certain actions (e.g., mitigation measures) are warranted.

The Department of the Treasury must submit a classified report to Congress that details the findings of the review and any action taken or recommended. To the extent practicable, the report must include an unclassified summary. (CFIUS is an interagency body that is chaired by the Secretary of the Treasury.)
